one_liner: Patient with two separate primary non-small cell lung carcinomas in the right upper lobe underwent right upper lobe wedge and lobectomy biopsies.

key_findings.name: Tumor size (wedge biopsy)
key_findings.interpretation: 0.8 cm poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma

procedures.name: Right upper lobe wedge lung biopsy
procedures.outcome: Negative for malignancy margins, 0.8 cm poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma

procedures.name: Right upper lobe resection
procedures.outcome: Negative for malignancy margins, 1.3 cm moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma

course.narrative: The patient underwent a right upper lobe wedge biopsy and right upper lobe lung resection along with lymph node samplings (10R, 4R, and subcarinal). Pathologic examination revealed two separate primary tumors in the right upper lobe: a 0.8 cm poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma and a 1.3 cm moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Arterial invasion was present in the resection specimen, but small vessel, lymphatic, and pleural invasions were not identified. All excised lymph nodes and excision margins were negative for malignancy.
